newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Pru ups Apple, cuts Dell.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Pru ups Apple, cuts Dell.

text.p: -- Prudential analyst Don Young said he raised his rating to buy from hold and bumped up his fiscal 1997 year estimate on Apple Computer Inc, but cut Dell Computer Corp to hold from buy and also lowered his fiscal 1998 estimate for the company.
-- Young said he cut his earnings estimate on Dell's fiscal year ending January 1998 to $5.25 from $5.50 per share.

-- The lowered opinion was the result of an in-depth study Young recently conducted among 35 of the Dell's largest corporate accounts, which he said suggested corporate demand for Dell servers was slower than he had forecast previously.
-- "The upside potential that we were hoping for in corporate sales of Pentium Pro and Windows NT is less than I expected," Young said of Dell's inroads into the corporate server computer market.
-- In light of his survey, Young said that, "On the server side, Dell is not well positioned to gain market share, at least not yet."

-- However, he noted that, "The good news is that Dell's desktop market share looks very, very strong going forward." He was referring to sales of individual desktop PCs as opposed to servers, which are used to manage groups of networked PCs.

-- Young said his cooler opinion of Dell reflected his view that PC makers with indirect sales were better positioned to benefit in coming quarters than companies such as Dell which use direct sales approaches.

-- "In general, we are seeing favorable conditions for the indirect," Young said. In particular, he said his view of Apple reflected the improving opportunities for PC makers relying on indirect sales efforts.
-- In addition, the Prudential analyst reaffirmed Compaq Computer Corp as the brokerage's "single best idea" among PC makers. He said Apple was its second best stock pick.

-- The analyst raised his estimate on Apple Computer for the fiscal year ending September 1997 to $1.40 per share from $1.10. He noted that $1.40 puts him at nearly double that of the current analysts' consensus for Apple's fiscal 1997 year.

In addition, he said he maintained his view the company would breakeven in the fourth quarter ended September 1996. The current analysts' estimates fall in the range of a loss of $0.05 to $0.20 for the recently ended quarter.
Despite his concern about direct PC sales, Young said he had reaffirmed his buy rating on Gateway 2000 Inc, which like Dell sells its PCs directly to customers.
